summary:
Partition by **colour range**, not by a pivot element: split colours `lo..hi` at `mid`, move colours `≤ mid` left
and the rest right with two pointers, then recurse on each side with its half of the colours. Each level is
O(n) and there are log k levels: O(n log k), with no counting array.

question.md:
Sort balls coloured `1..k` in **O(n log k)** without an extra array of size `k` (so no counting sort).

- **k can be as large as n**, in which case this is just O(n log n) sorting.
- **Up to 10⁵ balls.**

think.md:
`[3, 1, 4, 2, 4, 1, 3, 2]` with k = 4 → `[1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4]`.

The three-colour trick partitions around fixed values. Generalise it: split the colour range in half. All
colours `1..2` must end up left of colours `3..4`, so one two-pointer pass separates them. Each half is then the
same problem with half as many colours. After log k rounds, each range holds a single colour: sorted.

limits.md: Doesn't use the small number of colours: with k much smaller than n, splitting the colour range does only log k passes.

approaches.title: Split the colour range in half

idea.md: `sort(left, right, lo, hi)`: if the range has under 2 balls or one colour, stop. `mid = (lo + hi) / 2`. Two pointers: `i` skips colours `≤ mid` from the left, `j` skips colours `> mid` from the right; swap when both stop. Recurse on `[left, j]` with colours `lo..mid` and `[i, right]` with `mid+1..hi`.

build: Two-pointer split around the colour midpoint.

lines.text: A copy; start with all positions and all colours `1..k`.

notes.python: An explicit stack of (positions, colours) ranges instead of recursion.

lines.text: A range with fewer than two balls, or only one colour, is already sorted.

Split the colours at `mid`. `i` skips balls that belong left, `j` skips balls that belong right; when both stop, the two balls are on the wrong sides, so swap. Afterwards `[left, j]` holds colours `≤ mid` and `[i, right]` the rest.
Each side has half the colours: the recursion depth is log k.

complexity.md: **Time O(n log k):** every level of colour-halving touches each ball once. **Space O(log k)** for the recursion (or the stack).

steps.text: Positions 0..7, colours 1..4: colours ≤ 2 to the left (0..3), the rest to the right.
Positions 0..3, colours 1..2: colours ≤ 1 to the left (0..1), the rest to the right.
Positions 4..7, colours 3..4: colours ≤ 3 to the left (4..5), the rest to the right.

walk.title: Split the colour range in half: move colours 1..mid to the left and mid+1..k to the right with two pointers, then sort each side with its half of the colours.

takeaways.md:
- **Partition by value range** (binary search on the colours) generalises the three-colour flag to k colours.
- O(n log k) beats O(n log n) when k ≪ n, without a counting array.
- With O(k) extra space allowed, counting sort would be O(n + k).
